text: My education and qualifications are: I am running for City Council for good governance, for the environment, children and working families. I have worked as a community organizer and legislative leader on Barbara Boxer’s Senate and Barbara Lee’s State Senate campaigns, and coordinated the Kids First! Campaign, a $5.5 million youth fund. I co-founded Carnegie Library Innovation Hall Community Advisory Board and served on Rhythmix Cultural Works board. Fighting to protect our environment, I want to center city’s resources on the existential threat of climate change and sea level rise to protect our quality of life and ensure public safety. I led the effort to have City Council pass our Climate Emergency Declaration; founded 100K Trees for Humanity to plant over 400 trees for climate in our parks; and will support directing funds from the infrastructure bond to support our existing Climate Action and Shoreline Adaptation Plans. I supported our schools PTAs; served on AUSD Black Achievers Alliance, and Encinal HS Athletic Boosters. I will work for a more democratic and resilient community. I will work hard for our city as your City Council representative and continue to listen to, respect, and fight for your voice to be heard. www.amoswhite4alameda.com

text: President, Love Elementary School Site Council Secretary, Father

My education and qualifications are: My career is focused on understanding hard problems and solving them. At the U.S. Digital Service, an arm of The White House during the Biden administration, I worked on modernizing the IRS to be faster and easier to use. I led product teams at Google. I built an Emmy-winning education app used by millions of students, which Google acquired. I’m doing that same work here, as President of the Alameda Free Library Board and on Love Elementary’s School Site Council, where the accountability is a lot closer to home. I’ve also walked every street of this Island with my daughters. Along the way I talked with hundreds of Alamedans. What I heard was pride. People love this Island, and they know what could make it better. A universal call for safer, slower streets. Longtime residents who want to stay but are worried about getting priced out. Vacant storefronts draining the life from our downtowns. Climate change hitting our infrastructure, like the lagoons in Bay Farm. These are solvable. I’m running to solve them, and I’d love to earn your vote to do that work. thushanforalameda.com

text: My education and qualifications are: I love Alameda. We have the capacity and opportunity to care for our residents, businesses, nonprofits, neighbors, visitors and community in a manner that is unique and special because of the size of our city and the amount of people that contribute toward making Alameda a great place to live. I am an active community member, social work professional and mom to three Alameda Unified School District graduates. I am committed to youth, strengthening social services to support individuals and families in times of need and actively contributing to decisions that prioritize infrastructure improvements. As the former social services manager for the City of Alameda, I led youth and community groups like Alameda Collaboration for Children, Youth and their Families and worked across city departments to enhance social services and successfully deliver on projects that leveraged federal, state, county and city funding like Dignity Village and Queer Teen Alameda Center. I have extensive community engagement experience and most recently served as the executive director for Friends of the Alameda Free Library, where I remain an active volunteer. I know how the city works and I am a good listener. Vote for me and we can make Alameda a better community for all. marcie-johnson.com

text: My education and qualifications are: Alameda is the place I proudly call home and I believe we have an opportunity to thoughtfully plan for its future. It will take all of us working together to find creative solutions and move forward on the priorities that matter most. I have a background in energy and environmental policy, and after graduate school joined a clean tech startup advocating for increased sustainability. Since moving to Alameda, I’ve coached Alameda Little League and Alameda Youth Basketball and volunteered with local nonprofits supporting families and neighbors. I recently served four years on the Alameda County Mosquito Abatement District Board, helping promote public health and environmental protection. As a Coro Fellow in Public Affairs, I learned the importance of working with everyone in our community to develop effective, lasting solutions. That’s why Alameda is better together. Our greatest strength has always been the people who show up, support one another, and bring their unique experiences and perspectives. Together, we can create safe, accessible streets, support thriving business districts, and make thoughtful investments in the infrastructure that will serve Alameda for decades to come. I’m excited for the opportunity to work alongside each of you to help build Alameda’s future.
Candidate’s Statement CITY OF ALAMEDA FOR MEMBERS OF CITY COUNCIL

text: My education and qualifications are: I was born and raised in Alameda and graduated from Alameda High. Our kids graduated from Alameda High and our granddaughter is attending Alameda High. I am a member of the Board of Directors on the Alameda Citizens Taskforce. I will continue to preserve Alameda’s historic single family neighborhoods. I will continue to support the building of affordable housing in Alameda’s redevelopment areas. I will continue to support the excellence in our school system. My wife worked for the School District and our son is a teacher in the School District. I will continue helping build the upgrades to the school buildings. My company. Triple S Electric Co., wired up the Paden School remodel, the Washington School Remodel, the Height School remodel, the multipurpose buildings at Edison, Otis and Paden, and installed the underground at Ruby Bridges. I will continue to support the youth athletic programs like soccer and little league baseball. I will continue to work to complete the Veterans Center at the old Navy Base. I will continue to support our Police Department. I will support ending taxing of food eaten at restaurants.

text: My education and qualifications are: Dear Fellow Alamedans, my name is Maria Luisa Bondonno, and I seek your vote to serve as a Councilmember for the City of Alameda. My academic preparation includes a Bachelor of Arts in International Relations from San Francisco State University, a Master’s Degree in Communications from Cornell University, and a Juris Doctor from Hastings College of the Law. I began my career in public service as a Deputy Legislative Counsel for the State of California. I provided legal counsel to legislators, drafted approximately 100 bills per session, conducted legal research, prepared analytical memoranda, and testified before Legislative Committees—always advancing the public interest. In 2001, I joined the California Public Utilities Commission. I advised Supervisors, the General Counsel, and Commissioners on legal strategies affecting ratepayers. I attended closed sessions, presented oral arguments, developed litigation strategies for rehearing and appellate cases, authored Commission decisions, and represented the CPUC in appellate court. Throughout my career as a civil servant, my work has centered on rigorous legal analysis and the faithful protection of the public interest. I look forward to representing your interests to the best of my ability. I appreciate your support and your vote. Ademas, hablo espanol.
